tense noun

of a verb

also tenses, what tense is it?, verb tense, past tense, perfect tense, present tense, pluperfect, pluperfect tense

classical

Quint. 1.5.47: per tempora, ut in verbō … peccātur
Varr. LL 9.32 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 226, 249, 357

tempus, temporis n.

noun, third declension

a tense of the verb

The word for time is the word for tense, and the tenses are named with an adjective: tempus praesēns, praeteritum, futūrum. The question is Cujus temporis est?, what tense is it? (Traupman 241); in the present tense, tempore praesentī (227).

Examples

  • in participiō per genus et cāsum, ut in vocābulō, per tempora, ut in verbō, per numerum, ut in utrōque, peccātur

    in the participle one goes wrong in gender and case, as in a noun, in tense, as in a verb, and in number, as in bothQuint. 1.5.47

  • Cujus temporis est? — Praesentis.

    What tense is it? — The present.Traupman 241

  • quaedam verba etiam mūtantur, ut ferō in praeteritō

    some verbs even change, as ferō does in the past tenseQuint. 1.4.29 (Lewis & Short s.v. praetereō)

  • tempus praeteritum

    the past tenseTraupman 357

  • tempus praeteritum perfectum

    the perfect tenseTraupman 358

  • tempus plūsquamperfectum

    the pluperfect tenseTraupman 361

  • praesēns tempus

    the present tenseTraupman 364
